name: Small Multiples
summary: A Tufte-style grid of same-scale sparklines where one tile, Checkout conversion, breaks the pattern.
look: Near-white paper, hairline tile frames and thin teal sparklines on a shared dashed baseline; mono labels at 20 px. The single coral-framed tile is the only loud element.

components.name: Multiple tile
components.role: hairline frame, identical size and scale — the unit of the whole film

components.name: Shared baseline
components.role: dashed line at 100 % that every tile uses

components.name: Outlier frame
components.role: coral 4 px border + tint for the one tile that breaks

components.name: Event marker
components.role: vertical dashed line at 09:42 inside the tile

components.name: Mono tile label
components.role: 20 px metric name, top-left of every tile

components.name: Hairline rule
components.role: separates the grid from the decision strip

motion.name: Grid cascade
motion.how: tiles fade/scale 0.96 → 1 with a 0.03 s diagonal stagger, power2.out 0.35 s, total one bar at 120 BPM

motion.name: Rescale snap
motion.how: y-scales tween to the shared domain with expo.inOut 0.5 s landing on the drop

motion.name: Synchronized draw
motion.how: all sparklines stroke-dashoffset draw together over 4 beats (2 s), outlier breaks on beat 3 with a 0.1 s coral flash

story: Hook: 38 mismatched mini-charts, all different scales. Drop: they collapse into 14 same-scale tiles around a teal Acme tile. Proof: 12 labelled multiples, only Checkout conv. breaks −18% at 09:42 after deploy #2231, then Roll back. CTA: a calm strip of 14 tiles, Every metric. Every minute., Start free.
adapt: Put your product's real metrics or entities (services, regions, customers, jobs) into a same-scale grid; your anomaly is the one tile that breaks the pattern.

references.note: Tufte's small multiples: identical scales answer 'compared to what?'

fit.risk: Very calm; without strong timing the grid can feel like a static slide. Let the outlier tile do all the moving.
